transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello. It's nice to meet you too. 

Well, I came in because... I seem to be spending far too much of my day checking on things. I just keep opening the same folders, my desk drawers, and these labeled boxes I have, again and again. I have to make sure my important papers and keepsakes are exactly where I left them. And the frustrating thing is, I'll do this even when I just checked them a few minutes before. It's just getting to be too much to manage.
Do you experience the urge to check as unwanted and distressing?

Yes, it is very distressing. It's completely unwanted. I know I just checked, but... a thought will just keep needling me. I'll start thinking that maybe I accidentally threw away my late husband's old tax papers, or that I put a family recipe in the wrong box. Even when I know better, I just can't seem to let the thought pass without feeling like I've done something terribly careless. So I have to go check again.
Have you generally been preoccupied with order, rules, and control across many areas of your life for most of your adulthood?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I like things to be tidy, certainly, but I haven't spent my whole life obsessing over rules or needing to control everything. This... this constant checking and worrying about losing these specific things, it's really just something that's been happening lately. It's not how I've always been.
How long have these repeated checking thoughts and behaviors been occurring?

I'm not entirely sure exactly when it started, to be honest. It just sort of... crept up on me over time, and now it's just something I do every day. I don't really have a specific date or timeframe for you.
About how long have these checking thoughts and behaviors been happening—days, weeks, months, or years?

Well, it's certainly been longer than a few days or weeks. But... as for whether it's been several months or a few years, I honestly couldn't tell you. Like I said, it just sort of blended into my daily routine over time, so I really don't have a clear measure of it.

{"intent":"Determine whether the checking behaviors are performed in response to the intrusive thoughts, confirming both obsessions and compulsions.","question":"Do you check in order to relieve the distress caused by these intrusive worries?""}

Yes, exactly. I mean, the worry just builds up, and... I came in today because I spend far too much of my day just opening the same folders, the same drawers, and those labeled boxes again and again. I just have to make sure the important papers and keepsakes are where I left them. And... it's exhausting, because I do it even when I just checked them a few minutes before. It's the only way to get that awful feeling to settle down, just for a little bit.
When you are not checking, do the same unwanted worries about having misplaced or discarded those items keep returning on their own?

Yes, they do. Even when I know better, a thought will just keep needling me out of nowhere. I'll suddenly worry that I might have accidentally thrown away my husband's old tax papers, or... maybe I put a special family recipe in the wrong box. And I just can't seem to let it pass. The thought just stays there, and I end up feeling like I've done something terribly careless until I go back and look.
Do you feel driven to perform the checking even when you do not want to, rather than choosing to check as part of a routine?

Yes, I do. I really don't want to be doing it. Like I mentioned before, I spend so much of my day just opening those same folders and drawers and boxes over and over. I know I just looked at those papers and keepsakes a few minutes ago, but I just... I can't stop myself. It's not like a normal routine where you check the locks before bed. I feel like I absolutely have to do it, even when I'm tired of it.
About how much time do you spend checking each day?

I'm not exactly sure how to add it all up. I haven't really kept a strict clock on it. It just feels like it takes up a big chunk of my morning, and then it happens again in the afternoon. I couldn't give you an exact number of hours, just that it's... it's a lot of my day.
Have these unwanted thoughts and checking behaviors occurred on most days for at least two weeks?

Well, I couldn't say for certain if it's been exactly two weeks. I haven't really marked it on a calendar or kept track of the dates like that. I just know that lately... well, yes, it seems to happen on most days. But as for the exact number of weeks, I'm just not completely sure.
Have these unwanted thoughts and checking behaviors been occurring on most days for at least two weeks?

I believe I just answered that, didn't I? Like I mentioned a moment ago, yes, it is happening on most days. But I really don't keep a diary of these things, so I couldn't swear to you that it's been exactly fourteen days. It just feels like it's been going on for a while now.
Are the recurring worries themselves a significant problem for you, separate from the checking you do to relieve them?

Yes, they really are. Even when I know better, a thought will just keep needling me. I'll start worrying that I might have thrown away my husband's old tax papers, or... or maybe that I put a family recipe in the wrong box. 

I just can't seem to let it pass. The worry just sits there, and I end up feeling like I've done something terribly careless, even before I actually go to look. So, yes, the thoughts themselves are quite a problem.
Can you say with reasonable confidence that these unwanted thoughts and checking behaviors have been occurring for at least two weeks?

Doctor, I... I really don't know how else to answer that for you. We seem to keep going over this. As I've said, I haven't been keeping track of the exact days. 

I suppose, yes, if you just need to know if I'm reasonably confident, then it probably has been at least two weeks. It certainly feels like it's been going on for that long, if not longer. But I just don't have a firm timeline to give you.
Would you say that the intrusive worries and the repeated checking are both substantial and troublesome parts of what you are experiencing?

Yes, absolutely. I mean, the thoughts just won't leave me alone, and then... well, having to go check on things all the time is just exhausting. So, yes, they are both very troublesome to me. I wouldn't be here talking to you about it if they weren't.
